The files in this folder are weather model data of Deutscher Wetterdienst
(ICON-D2 and ICON-EU), processed and served by the software of
Open-Meteo.com. Deutscher Wetterdienst publishes the data under CC BY 4.0,
https://www.dwd.de/EN/service/legal_notice/legal_notice_node.html, and
Open-Meteo offers its data under CC BY 4.0,
https://open-meteo.com/en/licence. Credit: Weather data by Open-Meteo.com.
Datenbasis: Deutscher Wetterdienst, aufbereitet von Open-Meteo. The files
are not covered by the licence of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-21 between 09:25:15 and 09:25:17 UTC from
the forecast service of the owner's own installation, the stack in
deploy/ on the owner's Mac: the container image
ghcr.io/open-meteo/open-meteo:latest as built on 2026-11-03 (digest
sha256:bf94e8b39761b59a91bd04bb926b3834cad00eaf71f1aa64b2fd17fbe987846a),
with REMOTE_DATA_DIRECTORY pointing at Open-Meteo's open data on AWS,
https://openmeteo.s3.amazonaws.com/data/, which it reads when it is asked,
and API_SYNC_APIKEYS set. That is one of the two arrangements Open-Meteo
documents for running an instance of one's own. The instance was asked
from inside its container with curl. Open-Meteo's public API was not used.

Each file is the whole answer to one request of the adapter, unchanged:

    meta_icon_d2.json      GET /data/dwd_icon_d2_native/static/meta.json
    meta_icon_eu.json      GET /data/dwd_icon_eu_native/static/meta.json
    icon_d2_LAT_LON.json   GET /v1/forecast?latitude=LAT&longitude=LON
                           &models=dwd_icon_d2_native&hourly=...
    icon_eu_LAT_LON.json   the same with models=dwd_icon_eu_native

with the addresses the adapter builds (src/lib.rs, run_url and
series_url), the host apart: 45 hourly variables and forecast_days=3 for
ICON-D2, 44 hourly variables and forecast_days=4 for ICON-EU, and for
both wind_speed_unit=ms, timeformat=unixtime, elevation=nan and
cell_selection=nearest. An answer of ICON-D2 holds 72 hours and is about
19.5 kB; one of ICON-EU holds 96 hours and is about 25.1 kB.

The instance held the runs of 2026-11-21 06:00 UTC of both models,
ICON-D2's ready at 07:09:12 UTC and ICON-EU's at 09:14:18 UTC. ICON-EU's
is a main run, which reaches 78 hours hour by hour: to 2026-11-24 12:00
UTC, on the fourth of the days asked for. The two answers about the runs
were fetched again after the forecasts and were byte for byte the same.

They replace two earlier sets. The first, of 2026-11-19, had 44 and 43
variables; the 45th is sensible_heat_flux, the heat the ground gives to
the air, which the adapter began to ask for on 2026-11-21. The second, of
2026-11-21 between 00:25 and 00:28 UTC, was recorded with forecast_days=3
for both models and held ICON-EU's run of 2026-11-20 21:00 UTC, which
reaches 30 hours. It was replaced the same day, when the adapter began to
ask ICON-EU for four days: a recording with three days is no answer to
that request, and only a main run of ICON-EU has hours on the days after
the day after tomorrow. The moment was chosen for the days it holds: of
ICON-D2 all of the daylight of the 21st and the 22nd, of ICON-EU also the
23rd whole and the 24th until 12:00 UTC.

The five places: 47.70 N 11.80 E (east shore of the Tegernsee), 47.66 N
11.80 E (take-off on the Wallberg), 47.70 N 11.88 E and 47.68 N 11.90 E
(landing and take-off below the Jägerkamp), and 47.40 N 13.30 E (the
middle of the first region).

To record them again: run an Open-Meteo instance as deploy/README.md
describes, make the adapter's requests for these places and for the four
places of places/ against it, all in one go while it holds one run of
each model, replace the files, set the date and the runs in
src/fixtures.rs, then run the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and review
what changed. The tests pin the runs, the cells and a handful of values,
and so do tests of the server and of the apps, which read these answers
through the server's development mode and its golden files.

No file here was written by hand. The tests that need a damaged or partial
answer make one from these files and say what they change.

A value in these files is what a model computed for a grid cell. It is not
a measurement and no statement that a place can be flown.

The folder places/ holds answers to the adapter's requests for several
places at once, recorded in the same go from the same instance, on
2026-11-21 at 09:25:17 UTC:

    places/meta_icon_d2.json   GET /data/dwd_icon_d2_native/static/meta.json
    places/meta_icon_eu.json   GET /data/dwd_icon_eu_native/static/meta.json
    places/icon_d2.json        GET /v1/forecast?latitude=47.6000,47.6000,
                               47.7000,47.7000&longitude=11.8000,11.9000,
                               11.8000,11.9000&models=dwd_icon_d2_native
                               &hourly=...&forecast_days=3
                               &elevation=nan,nan,nan,nan
                               &cell_selection=nearest
    places/icon_eu.json        the same with models=dwd_icon_eu_native
                               and forecast_days=4

with the address the adapter builds (src/lib.rs, series_url) for the four
points of a grid of a tenth of a degree around the Tegernsee and the
Spitzingsee. They are of the same runs as the files above, and the two
answers about the runs are byte for byte the same as those above; they
were fetched again after the forecasts and had not changed. The third of
the four places, 47.7 N 11.8 E, is the first of the five above, and its
answer here is value for value its answer there, for both models. The set
these replace, of 2026-11-21 between 03:20 and 03:21 UTC, was of a later
run of ICON-D2 than the single places then were, and its answer about
that run differed from theirs. The two sets are still kept as two, each
with its own answers about the runs, for two fetchers.

What was seen of an instance from the same image on 2026-11-21, when the
set before this one was recorded, and is written down in
docs/data-sources.md: it answers several places with a JSON list, one
answer per place in the order asked, each the same as the answer for that
place alone (compared value for value for these four, ICON-D2), and every
answer but the first carries its position as location_id. One
elevation=nan for four places is refused (400, "Parameter 'elevation' must
have the same number of elements as coordinates"); cell_selection takes
one value for all places and refuses a list.

The server's development mode makes its thermal map from the files in
places/, and its forecasts for a place from the files above.
